translations.text: The proverbs of Solomon son of David, who reigned in Israel.
To know wisdom and instruction, and to understand words of understanding.
To receive [?] sayings and explanations of riddles, to understand true righteousness and make judgment upright.
So that I may give understanding to the simple, and perception and thought to a young child.
For the wise person who listens to these things will become wiser, and the person with understanding will gain guidance.
He will understand a parable and a hidden saying, the words of the wise and their riddles.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of God, and understanding is good for everyone who practices it. The beginning of perception is love for God, but the ungodly will despise wisdom and instruction.
Listen, my son, to your father's instruction, and do not abandon your mother's rules.
For you will receive a graceful crown upon your head and a gold necklace around your neck.
My son, do not let sinful people lead you astray.
And do not consent if they urge you, saying, “Come with us and take part in this murder.”
“Let us lie in wait unjustly for a righteous person.”
“Let us swallow him alive like the underworld, and remove his memory from the earth. Let us acquire his many possessions and fill our houses with plunder.”
“Cast your lot with us, and let us have one shared purse.”
My son, do not walk along the road with them, but turn your feet away from their paths.
For their feet run toward evil, and they hurry to shed blood.
For nets are not spread for birds in vain.
For they take part in bloodshed, gathering evil upon themselves.
These are the paths of everyone who commits sins. The downfall of lawless people is terrible, for they will destroy their own lives through their folly.
Wisdom is praised in the streets, and she speaks openly in the public squares. She is proclaimed on the heights of the walls.
She speaks boldly at the gates of the cities,
saying, “As long as the simple are deprived of righteousness, they will not feel shame. The foolish desire disgrace. When they became ungodly, they hated perception and became hostile to rebukes.”
“Look, I will speak to you the word of my breath, and I will teach you my word.”
“Since I called to you and you did not listen to me, and I spread out my words and you paid no attention,”
“but you rejected my counsel and refused to listen to my rebukes,”
“I too will therefore laugh at your destruction, and I will rejoice over you when destruction comes upon you.”
And if turmoil overtakes you suddenly, and ruin comes upon you like a storm, or if destruction comes upon you, and distress and trouble come upon you,
then you will cry out to me, but I will not listen to you. The wicked will seek me and will not find me.
For they hated wisdom and did not choose devotion to God for themselves.
And they would not pay attention to my advice, but turned away from my rebukes.
Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way and be filled with their own wickedness.
For because they oppressed the little ones, they will be killed, and scrutiny will destroy the ungodly.
But whoever listens to me will rest securely in peace and will remain without fear of any evil.
My son, if you receive the words of my commandment and treasure them within you, your ear will listen to wisdom.
And you will apply your heart to understanding and give it to your son for instruction.
For if you call out to wisdom and call for discernment with a loud voice,
and seek it like treasures of silver and search for it eagerly,
then you will understand devotion to God and find holy discernment, so that your feet do not stumble.
For God will give you wisdom from his mouth, along with discernment and understanding.
And he stores up help for the righteous, strengthening their ways.
He guards the paths of truth and watches over the paths of the merciful.
This, then, is how you will understand righteousness and truth all the more. For truth has straight paths, and the paths of the good are straight.
For if wisdom enters your heart and you consider discernment good for your soul,
good counsel will guard you, and holy thought will watch over you.
For he will rescue you from an evil path and from a person who speaks no truth.
O you who abandon the straight paths and choose paths of darkness for yourselves,
who rejoice over evildoers and laugh over evil,
whose paths are crooked and whose tracks are twisted,
so that you distance yourself and become a stranger to the judgment of the righteous.
My son, do not let evil counsel overtake you, which abandons instruction from its youth and forgets the holy covenant.
For it has set its house beside death, and its paths are with the people in the underworld.
None who gather around it will return, and they will not reach the paths of life. Instead, they will [?], for the years of life will not reach them.
For if they had walked on the good paths, they would have found the paths of the righteous smooth.
The good will live on the earth, and the innocent will remain on it, for the upright will live in the land, and the holy will remain on it.
The ungodly will be overthrown from the earth, and the lawless will be uprooted from it.
My son, do not forget my laws, and let your heart keep my words.
For they will add to you a long life, years of life, and peace.
Do not let mercy, faithfulness, and truth leave you. Bind them around your neck.
Gain favor and a good reputation before the Lord and before people.
Trust in God with your whole heart, and do not exalt yourself because of your wisdom.
Reveal her in all your ways, so that she may straighten your paths and your foot may not stumble.
Do not consider yourself wise on your own. Instead, fear God and turn away from every evil.
Then there will be healing for your body and care for your bones.
My son, honor God with the proceeds of your honest labor, and give him the firstfruits of your righteous harvest.
So that your storehouses may be filled with grain and your vats may be filled with wine.
My son, do not lose heart under the Lord’s discipline, and do not grow weary when you are rebuked by him.
For God disciplines the one he loves, and he scourges every son he will accept. For he will afflict you and set you on your feet again.
Blessed is the person who has found wisdom, and the person who has found understanding.
For working with her is better than treasures of gold and silver.
She is more precious than genuine gemstones. Nothing evil will oppose her. She reveals herself to everyone who approaches her, and all precious things are unworthy of her.
Long life and years of life are in her right hand, and glory and wealth are in her left. Righteousness comes from her mouth, and she bears law and mercy on her tongue.
Her paths are good paths, and all her ways are peaceful.

She is a tree of life for everyone who trusts in her, and she is firmly established over those who establish themselves upon her, like those firmly established upon the Lord. 19. God laid the foundations of the earth through wisdom and prepared the heavens through his understanding.
The depths opened through understanding, and the clouds poured down dew.
My son, do not become slack, but keep my counsel and my thought.
So that your soul may live and grace may be upon your neck. Then there will be healing for your flesh and care for your bones.
So that you may walk confidently and peacefully in all your ways, and your foot will not stumble.
And when you lie down, you will forget and be at ease.
And you will not be afraid of a terror coming upon you or of the coming calamity of the ungodly.
For God will be on all your paths and will make your feet firm so that you will not waver.
Do not stop doing good to the needy when your hand has the means to help.
Do not say, “Go away and come back, and tomorrow I will give to you,” when you have the means to do good. For you do not know what tomorrow will bring.
Do not plan evil against your companion who is at ease and trusts you.
Do not be hostile to anyone without cause, so that he will not harm you.
Do not adopt the violence of evil people, and do not envy their ways.
For a lawless person is unclean before God, and he gathers with the righteous.
God’s curse is in the houses of the ungodly.
But the homes of the righteous will be blessed. God will oppose the proud, but he will give grace to the humble.
The wise will inherit glory, but fools will choose great disgrace for themselves.
Listen, my children, to your father’s instruction, and pay attention so that you may understand a thought.
For it is a good gift that I am giving you. Do not abandon my word.
For I too was a child, obeying my father, and my mother loved me.
They in turn taught me, saying:
“Let our word become firmly established in your heart. Keep my commandments and do not forget them, and do not forget the words of my mouth.
Do not abandon it, so that it may welcome you; love it, so that it may guard you.
The beginning of wisdom is this: acquire knowledge, and acquire understanding with everything you have.
Turn toward it so that it may exalt you; honor it so that it may welcome you.
Then it will place a crown of grace on your head and protect you with a crown of delight.
Listen, my son, and accept my words, so that you may have many paths of life.
For I am teaching you the ways of wisdom and setting you on straight paths.
For when you walk, your paths will not be blocked before you. If you run—if you run, you will not grow weary.
Hold firmly to my instruction; do not abandon it. Keep it for yourself throughout your life.
Do not walk on the paths of sinners.
Do not enter with them into the place where they gather. Keep your distance and turn away from them.
For they will not sleep unless they have done evil; for slumber has gone far from them, and they do not sleep.
For they are nourished by food of wickedness, and they get drunk on the wine of sinners.
But the paths of the righteous shine like the light, for they go on shining until the day is complete.
But the paths of the ungodly are darkness, and they do not know how they stumble.
My son, pay attention to my words, and turn your ear toward my corrections.
So that your springs do not dry up, keep these things in your heart.
For they are life to those who find them and healing for the body.
Guard your heart with every care, for paths of life come from these things.
Put a crooked mouth far from you, and let unjust lips be far away from you.
Let your eyes look at what is straight, and let your eyelids look toward what is true.
Make straight paths for your feet, and straighten your ways.

Do not turn to the right or to the left, but turn your feet away from every evil path. For God knows the paths on the right, but those on the left are crooked. He will straighten your paths and guide your journeys in peace.
My son, pay attention to my wisdom, and turn your ear toward my words.
So that you may preserve good judgment, I instruct you in the understanding expressed by my lips.
Do not pay attention to an evil woman, for honey drips from the lips of a prostitute, who will sweeten your throat for a moment.
Afterward you will find her more bitter than wormwood and sharper than a two-edged sword.
For in her foolishness her feet lead those who use her down to death, to Hades, and her steps are not firm.
For she does not walk on the paths of life. Her paths are unsettled and hidden.
Now then, my son, listen to me, and do not turn away from my words.
Let your path stay far from her, and do not approach the doors of her house.
So that you do not give your life to others and your years to the merciless.
So that others do not satisfy themselves with your strength, and your hard-earned gains do not go into other people's houses.
Afterward you will regret it in your old age, when the flesh of your body wastes away.
Then you will say, “Why did I not want to be taught, and why did my heart turn away from correction?”
And you will say, “I did not listen to the voice of the one teaching me, and I did not turn my ear toward it.
I almost came into every kind of evil in the midst of the assemblies and the crowds.”
Drink water from your own vessels and from the wells of your own spring.
Do not let your waters flow outside your spring, but let your waters flow through your streets.
Let it belong to you alone. Do not let any stranger share it with you.
Let the spring of your water belong to you alone, and rejoice with the wife of your youth.

Let the deer of your affection and the foal of your favor talk with you. Let the woman who is yours take the lead over you and stay with you at all times, for as you walk in her companionship, you will flourish.
Do not spend much time with a foreign woman, and do not make your way into the arms of a woman who is not yours.
For a person's ways are before God's eyes, and he watches all their ways.
Lawless deeds trap a person, and each person is bound by the cords of his sins.
This person will die with the multitudes because he lacks instruction. He was cast out because of his excessive pleasure, and he perished because of his foolishness.
My son, if you stand as guarantor for your friend, you will give your hand to your enemy.
For a person's own lips are a powerful trap for him, and he is ruined by the words of his mouth.

My son, do what I command you, so that you may live. For you have fallen into the hands of evil people because of your friend. Do not be careless, but plead with your fellow citizen for whom you have stood as guarantor.
Do not give sleep to your eyes, and do not give rest to your eyelids.
So that you may escape like a gazelle from traps and like a bird from a snare.
Go to the ant, you lazy person. Follow its ways eagerly and become wiser than it.
For it has no field, no one to compel it, and no master over it.

See how it prepares its food in summer and increases its stores at harvest. Or go to the bee and learn its industriousness and how wisely it does its work. Its labors are offered to kings and people for their relief. It is honored by everyone and loved. Although it is weak in strength, it has honored wisdom and advanced.
How long will you lie there, you lazy person? When will you rise from sleep?
You sleep a little, you sit a little, you rest a little, and for a little while your hands support you beneath your chest.

Afterward, poverty comes to you like an evil person walking with you on a road, and need like a swift runner. But if you are not lazy, your harvest comes like a spring, and need will flee from you like an evil person.
A foolish and lawless person walks on evil paths.
And he winks with his eye, signals with his foot, and gives instructions through gestures of his fingers.
His crooked heart thinks of evil things at all times. A person like this causes disturbances in cities.

Therefore his destruction is coming suddenly: a crushing blow and a shattering beyond healing. Because he rejoices in every evil deed that God hates, he will be shattered because of the impurity of his soul.
There are six things that the Lord has hated, and seven are an abomination to his soul.
The eye of a scoffer, a tongue of injustice, hands that shed the blood of the righteous,
a heart that thinks evil thoughts, feet that hurry to do evil.
An unjust witness kindles lies and sends malicious conflict among brothers.
My son, keep your father's laws, and do not abandon your mother's instructions.
Bind them firmly to your soul and make them a necklace around your neck.
When you walk, take it with you, and let it be with you. When you sleep, let it guard you, so that when you rise, it will talk with you.
For the good commandment gives light, and the law is a light on the road, for instruction corrects the ways of life.
So that it may protect you from a woman who is not yours, and from the slanderous tongue of strangers.
Do not let the beauty you desire overcome you. Do not let yourself be ensnared through your eyes, and do not let her capture you with her eyelids.
For the price of a prostitute is only a single loaf of bread, but a woman hunts for the precious lives of men.
Can anyone wrap burning coals in his lap without burning his clothes? 28
Or can anyone walk on fiery coals without scorching his feet?
So it is with someone who goes in to a married woman: he will not be free from sin, nor will anyone who touches her.
It is not surprising if someone is caught stealing, for he steals to satisfy his hungry soul.
For if he is caught, he will repay them sevenfold and give all his possessions to save himself.
But the adulterer, through his own lack of sense, brings destruction on his own life.
He will bear sorrows and insults, and his disgrace will never be erased.
For her husband's anger is full of jealousy, and he will show no mercy on the day of revenge.
He will not quiet his hostility for any ransom, nor will he relent for many gifts.
My son, keep my words and store my commandments with you. Honor God so that you may become strong, and fear no one but him.
Keep my commandments so that you may live. Put my words on your fingers like the pupils of your eyes.
Write them on the tablet of your heart.
Say that wisdom is your sister and understanding is your relative, and acquire her for yourself.
She will protect you from an evil woman who is not yours, when she speaks with charming words.
For she looks out through the window of her house into the streets.
The young man she sees is senseless and lacks instruction.
He walks near the street corners by her house.
He speaks in the darkness at evening, as the place grows dark in the evening gloom.
The woman meets him dressed like a prostitute, the woman who sets young men's hearts aflutter.
She is frivolous and wanton, and her feet do not stay in her house.
For sometimes she wanders outside, and sometimes she lies in wait at every corner in the streets.
Then she takes hold of him and kisses him, and with a shameless face she says to him:
“I have a peace offering; today I will fulfill my vows.
That is why I came out to meet you, longing to see your face, and I found it.”
I have stretched linen bands across my bed and spread it with double-sided rugs from Egypt.
I have sprinkled my bed with saffron and my house with cinnamon.
Come, let us enjoy each other's company until morning. Come, let us delight in love.
For my husband is not at home; he has gone on a distant journey.
He has a purse in his hands, and he will return home after many days.
She led him astray with a long persuasive speech. She bound him with flatteries and drew him away with her lips.
He followed her in agitation, like a calf being led to slaughter, and like a dog hurrying to be put in a collar,
or like a deer pierced in the liver by an arrow. He hurries like a bird into a trap, not knowing that it is the place of his ruin.
Now then, my son, listen to me and pay attention to the words of my mouth.
Do not let your heart turn toward her paths.
For she has wounded many and cast them down, and those she has killed are beyond counting.
Her paths lead to the houses of the underworld; they descend to the chambers of death.
But you, proclaim wisdom, so that understanding will listen to you.
For she is on the high hills, and she stands in the middle of the roads.
She takes her place beside the gates of the powerful, and they praise her at the entrance.
“I call to you, people, and I tell you my teaching, children of humankind.
You simple people, understand wisdom. You fools, set your minds to it.
Listen to me, for I will speak words of instruction, and I will declare what is right with my lips.
For my mouth speaks of faithfulness, but lying lips are unclean in my sight.
All the words of my mouth are righteous; none of them is twisted or crooked.
They are all plain to those who understand, and straightforward to those who want to gain discernment.
Seek gain from instruction, not silver, and from knowledge rather than choice gold. Choose understanding rather than precious gold.
For wisdom is better than precious stones, and nothing valuable can equal her.
I, Wisdom, created counsel. I established discernment and thought for myself.
Devotion to God hates evil, and it hates insolence, arrogance, evil paths, and a lying mouth. Counsel and steadfastness are mine.
Understanding is mine; strength is mine.”
Through me kings reign, and through me the powerful rule the earth.
Through me the great become greater, and through me rulers hold power over the earth.
I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find me.
For I possess wealth and glory, abundant possessions and righteousness.
What I produce is better for you than gold and genuine precious stones, and my yield is better than choice silver.
I walk along paths of righteousness and travel along the paths of truth,
so that I may distribute wealth among those who love me and fill their storehouses with good things. When I tell you about daily events, I will remember to recount things from eternity.
God created at the beginning of his ways, for his works, before he made anything.
And he established me before the ages, in the beginning.
Before he made the earth, he brought me forth, before the deep,
before the springs of water came forth, before he made the mountains firm and shaped the earth and the inhabited world. He brought me forth before every hill.
God made heaven and earth and the farthest reaches of the earth inhabited beneath heaven.
When he was preparing heaven, I was with him, and when he was spreading out his throne over the winds,
and when he was securing the springs beneath heaven and making the clouds above firm,
and when he was laying the foundations of the earth,
I was with him, preparing things for him. It was I in whom he delighted. I rejoiced daily before him, at all times.
And he rejoiced when he completed the inhabited world, and he rejoiced over humankind. His delights make people rejoice.
Now then, my children, listen to me.
Pay attention to the words of my instruction, so that you may live a long life and become wise. Do not disregard my rebukes.
Blessed is the person who will listen to me, and the person who will keep to my paths, keeping watch daily at my doors and guarding the doorposts of my entrances.
For my paths are paths of life, and the will is prepared by the Lord. Cheerfulness comes from God, along with every excellent deed.
Those who sin against me will harm their own souls, and those who hate me are companions of death.
Wisdom built herself a house and made seven pillars firm.
She slaughtered her animals, mixed her wine in a bowl, and prepared her table.
She sent out her servants, calling out with a loud proclamation over her bowl, saying,
“Let the foolish person among you turn to me.” And she said to those who lack instruction,
“Come, eat some of my bread and drink my wine, which I have mixed.
Leave foolishness behind so that you may live. Seek understanding so that you may survive, and direct understanding aright. Think about instruction on a straight path.”
Whoever teaches the wicked will bring insults upon himself. An insult will come upon the wicked through what they hope for. The rebukes belonging to the ungodly are blemishes.
Do not rebuke the wicked, or they will hate you. Rebuke a wise person, and he will love you.
Give a wise person an opportunity, and he will become wiser. Instruct a righteous person, and he will increase his knowledge.
Devotion to God is the beginning of wisdom, and the understanding of the holy ones is knowledge. Understanding the law is good judgment.
For in this way you will live a long life, and years of life will be added to you.

My son, if you become wise, you will benefit yourself and your neighbor. But if you become wicked, you alone will draw evil upon yourself. Whoever establishes himself on lies feeds on winds and pursues flying birds. For he has abandoned the paths of his vineyard and forgotten the paths of his own field. He walks through a waterless desert and through a barren land in thirst, gathering blight into his hands.
There is a brazen and foolish woman who will lack bread; she knows no shame.
She sat at the doorway of her house, on a seat, openly visible in the streets.
She calls to those passing by and those going straight along their paths, saying:
“Whoever among you is foolish, let him turn aside to me. I give instructions to those who lack learning, saying:
‘Eat bread in secret with delight, and stolen water is sweet.’”

But he does not know that people die beside her, and that she draws them into the midst of Hades. Instead, flee far away and do not linger in her place, and do not fix your eyes on her. For this is how you will drink water that is not yours and cross a foreign river. Keep away from water that is not yours, and do not drink from a foreign spring, so that you may live a long time. For whoever approaches her will go down to Hades, but whoever keeps away will be saved and live a long time, and years of life will be added to him.
A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son is a sorrow to his mother.
Treasures will not benefit the lawless, but righteousness rescues from death.
The Lord will not let a righteous person die of hunger, but he will take away the life of the ungodly.
Poverty humbles a person, but the hand of the strong makes rich. An instructed son will become wise, and he will use the fool as a servant.
A wise son will be safe in the heat, but a lawless son will sleep during the harvest. He will gather during the summer, but the disgraceful person will sleep during the harvest.
God’s blessing rests upon the heads of the righteous, but untimely sorrow will cover the mouths of the ungodly.
The remembrance of the righteous is a good reputation, but the name of the ungodly will be extinguished.
The person who is wise at heart will accept the commandment, but the fool will be caught by his lips. The unruly person whose lips speak perversely will fall.
Whoever walks with prudence walks securely, but whoever turns aside from his paths will be exposed.
Whoever winks deceitfully will bring sorrow upon people, but whoever rebukes openly will bring them peace.
The fountain of life is in the hand of the righteous, but destruction will cover the mouth of the ungodly.
Hatred stirs up conflict, but friendship will cover all who do not commit violence.
Whoever brings wisdom out of his mouth strikes a foolish person with a rod.
The wise will conceal insults, but the mouth of an unruly person will bring destruction near.
A rich person’s possessions are a fortified city, but poverty is the ruin of the ungodly.
The deeds of the righteous produce life, but the fruits of the ungodly are sins.
Instruction guards the paths of life, but instruction that has not been corrected leads astray.
Truthful lips conceal their hostility, but those who utter curses are foolish.
Through excessive talking you will not escape sin, but if you restrain your lips, you will be wise.
The tongue of the righteous is choice silver, but the heart of the ungodly will fail.
The lips of the righteous know lofty things, but fools will die in want.
God’s blessing is wealth, and no sorrow of heart is added to it.
A fool does wicked things for amusement, but wisdom produces understanding in a person.
The ungodly perish in destruction. What the ungodly fear will come upon them, but the desires of the righteous are accepted.
The ungodly will perish in a passing storm, but the righteous will withdraw from it and be safe forever.
Like vinegar that makes the teeth ache, and like smoke in the eyes, so is lawlessness to those who practice it.
Devotion to God adds length to life, but the years of the ungodly will be shortened.
Joy remains with the righteous, but the hope of the ungodly will perish.
The way of the Lord is the exaltation of the holy person. But the way of the Lord is a terror to those who practice lawlessness and destruction to those who do evil.
The righteous will never retreat, but the ungodly will not remain on the earth.
The mouth of the righteous will speak wisdom, but the tongue of the unjust will perish.
The lips of righteous people know gracious things, but the mouth of the ungodly will be destroyed.
Dishonest measures are detestable before the Lord, but an honest measure pleases him.
Where disgrace enters, contempt is there too, but the mouth of the humble will reflect on wisdom.
The prudence of the upright will guide them. When a righteous person dies, people mourn him, but they clap their hands at the destruction of the ungodly and rejoice over it.
Wealth will be of no benefit on the day of wrath, but righteousness rescues from death.
The righteousness of the holy person will straighten his paths, but the unjust person will fall into wickedness.
The righteousness of upright people will save them, but the lawless will perish in their wickedness.
When a good person dies, his hope does not perish, but the boasting of the ungodly will perish.
The righteous escape troubles, but the sinner will be put in their place.
There is a trap for their fellow citizens in the mouth of the lawless, but the understanding of the righteous is upright.
Cities are exalted through the blessings of the righteous.
But they are destroyed through the mouth of the ungodly.
A foolish person despises his fellow townspeople, but a wise person keeps silent.
A person with a double tongue reveals plans in an assembly, but someone faithful to his word keeps matters secret.
Those who have no guidance fall like leaves, but safety lies in abundant counsel.
The wicked person thinks of evil when he encounters the righteous, and he hates acts of steadfastness.
A gracious woman raises her husband's honor, but a woman who hates righteousness is a throne of disgrace. The lazy will lack wealth, but the diligent will become established in wealth.
A merciful person does good to his own soul, but a merciless person will destroy his own body. The ungodly person does unjust deeds.
But the person who sows righteousness works toward faithfulness. The seed of the righteous is a true reward.
A righteous son is born for life, but the pursuit of the ungodly leads to death.

The stubborn are unclean before God. Someone whose path is crooked is an abomination to the Lord, but everyone whose path is pure is acceptable to him, for his desire is for everyone who remains pure in their path.
Someone who joins another in injustice will not be free from suffering, but someone who produces righteousness will receive a reward for faithfulness.
Like a ring in a pig's snout, so is the beauty of an evil-minded woman.
Every desire of the righteous is good, but the hope of the ungodly will perish.
There is someone who distributes his own possessions, and they increase for him. There are others who gather possessions for themselves, yet remain in need.
Every soul that is blessed flourishes, but an angry person is no good.
The crowd curses someone who hoards grain, but a blessing comes upon the head of someone who gives.
Someone who thinks of good things seeks good favor, but evil things will overtake those who seek them.
Someone who trusts in wealth will fall, but someone who has mercy on the poor will be called blessed. Someone who builds his house through injustice will leave sorrows to his children.
But someone who does not live in harmony with his household will inherit winds. The foolish person will become the wise person's servant.
A tree of life comes from the fruit of righteousness, but the souls of the lawless will be killed through rashness.
If the righteous person will barely be saved, then where will the sinner and the ungodly person appear?
Someone who loves instruction loves understanding, but someone who hates rebukes is senseless.
The person who has found favor before God is good, but a person who plans evil acts lawlessly.
No one will become established through lawlessness, but the roots of the righteous will not be uprooted.
A capable woman is her husband's crown. Like a worm in wood and a moth in a garment, so an evil-minded woman will destroy her husband.
The thoughts of the righteous are just judgments, but the ungodly steer their course through deceit.
The mouth of the righteous will save them, but the mouth of the ungodly is deceitful.
The ungodly will perish wherever they turn, but the houses of the righteous will endure.
The townspeople praise the mouth of an intelligent person, but they mock the fainthearted.
A person who serves himself and is held in contempt is better than someone who honors himself but lacks bread.
The righteous person has compassion on the lives of his animals, but the mercies of the ungodly are merciless.

Anyone who works his land will have his fill of bread, but those who chase worthless things lack understanding. Anyone who takes pleasure in wine-drinking places will leave disgrace in his dwelling places.
The desires of the ungodly are evil, but the roots of godly people are firmly established.

The sinner will fall into a trap because of the testimony of his lips, but the righteous person will escape these things. Mercy will be shown to someone who is completely confident, but someone who waits at the gates will sustain lives.
A person's soul will be filled with good things from the fruit of his mouth, and he will be given the reward of his lips.
The ways of fools are straight in their own eyes, but the wise listen to advice.
A fool expresses his anger every day, but a wise person conceals his disgrace.
The righteous person speaks openly of what is trustworthy, but the testimony of an unjust witness is deceit.
There are people whose words are like those who stab with a sword, but the tongues of the wise bring healing.
Truthful lips set testimony straight, but a hasty witness has an unjust tongue.
Deceit is in the heart of someone who plans evil things, but those who counsel peace will rejoice.
No injustice will please the righteous person, but the ungodly will die in evil.
Lying lips are detestable to the Lord, but anyone who acts faithfully is acceptable to him.
A wise person is a throne of understanding, but the heart of a fool will persist in curses.
The hand of the chosen will gain authority, but the deceitful will be subject to tribute. The heart of a fool will persist in evil things.
A frightening word troubles a person's heart, but a good answer makes him glad.
A righteous person reveals himself to his companion, and the counsels of godly people are judgments, but the way of the ungodly will lead them astray.
The deceitful person will not catch any game, but a holy person is an honorable treasure.
Life is on the paths of righteousness, but the paths of those who plan evil lead to death.
A wise son listens to his father, but a disobedient son is headed for destruction.
The good person will eat from the fruit of righteousness, but the souls of lawless people will die before their time.
Anyone who guards his mouth guards his soul, but anyone who is reckless with his lips will bring trouble on himself.
Every lazy person is full of desires, but the hands of the strong are firm.
The righteous person hates an unjust word, but the ungodly person will be put to shame and have no confidence.
Righteousness protects the innocent, but sin makes the deceitful ungodly.
Some make themselves out to be rich when they have nothing, while others humble themselves though they possess great wealth.
A person's wealth is the ransom for his life, but the poor person does not have to bear a threat.
The righteous always have light, but the light of the ungodly will go out. Deceitful souls wander in sins, but the righteous are compassionate and show mercy.
The wicked person does evil with insolence, but those who know righteousness are wise.
Wealth that people hurry to acquire through lawlessness will diminish, but wealth gathered through devotion to God will increase.
The person who first offers heartfelt help is better than the one who promises and gives hope. For a good desire becomes a tree of life.
The person who despises a matter will be despised, but the person who fears the commandment will be safe. Nothing good will come to a deceitful son, but a wise servant will have success in his work.
There is a fountain of life in the paths of wisdom, but the fool will die in a trap.
Good understanding brings favor, but the paths of the lawless are destruction.
Every shrewd person acts with deliberation, but the fool displays his wickedness.
A stubborn messenger will fall into trouble, but a faithful messenger brings healing.
Instruction removes poverty and disgrace, but the person who pays attention to correction will receive honor.

The desires of the godly bring joy to their souls, but the desires of the ungodly are far from knowledge. The defilements of the ungodly are far from understanding, and the ungodly will curse the godly.
If you walk with wise people, you will become wise, but the person who walks with fools will be exposed. The righteous will live in peace.
Evil will pursue sinners, but good things will overtake the righteous.
The righteous person will distribute to his grandchildren, and the wealth of the ungodly is gathered for the righteous.
The strong will enjoy ease in wealth for many years, but some have perished immediately.
The person who spares his rod hates his son, but the person who loves his own son will discipline him diligently.
When the righteous person eats, he satisfies his soul, but the souls of the ungodly will suffer want.
Wise women build houses, but the foolish woman will tear hers down with her own hands.
The person who walks uprightly fears God, but the person whose paths are crooked will receive disgrace.
A rod of disgrace is in the mouths of fools, but the lips of the wise will protect [?].
The feeding troughs are empty where there are no cattle, but the strength of the cattle is evident where there is abundant produce.
A faithful witness will not lie, but an unjust witness spews lies.
You will seek wisdom among evil people and will not find it, but understanding is readily available to the wise.
Everything opposes the foolish person, but the lips of the wise are weapons of understanding. But the lips of the wise are weapons of understanding.
The wisdom of sensible people will understand their ways, but foolishness will teach through deception.
The houses of the lawless deserve cleansing, but the houses of the righteous are choice.
The heart of a perceptive person is a sorrow to his soul, but when he rejoices, sorrow does not mingle with him.
The houses of the ungodly will be destroyed, but the tents of the righteous will stand.
There is a way that a person thinks is straight, but its end reaches the pit of Hades.
Sorrow does not mingle with happiness, but the end of joy leads to grief.
The hardhearted person will be filled with his own ways alone, but the holy person with his own thoughts.
The simple person believes every word, but the wise person is cautious.
When the wise person is afraid, he turns away from evil, but the fool stubbornly involves himself in it.
Someone quick to anger acts foolishly, but a wise person bears a great deal.
Evil will be apportioned to fools, but the wise hold on to understanding.
The wicked will fall before the good, and the ungodly will serve at the gates of the righteous.
Friends hate their poor friends, but the rich have many friends. The sinner scorns his friends.
Whoever insults the poor sins, but whoever has mercy on the poor is blessed.

Those who go astray work at evil. The merciful are counselors of good, but counselors of violence go astray in their counsel. Mercy and truth belong to those who do good. Those who do evil do not know mercy and faithfulness, but those who do good possess mercy and faithfulness.
There is wisdom in everyone who takes care, but the person who takes it easy and does not exert himself will lack wisdom.
Wealth is the crown of the wise, but the dwelling place of fools is bad.
A trustworthy witness saves souls from evil, but deceit kindles lies.
Hope for strength lies in the fear of the Lord. Devotion to God is a firm support, and he will leave his children a secure foundation for life.
The Lord's command is a spring of life, and it turns them away from the snare of death.
A king's glory lies in a great multitude, but a ruler's ruin lies in the destruction of his people.
A patient person has much wisdom, but a short-tempered person is exceedingly foolish.
A person who does not become angry is a physician to his own heart, but a perceptive heart is a moth to the bones.
Whoever oppresses a poor person insults his Maker, but whoever honors him has mercy on a poor person.
The ungodly person will be humbled through his wickedness, but whoever trusts in his own purity is righteous.
Truth abounds in a person's good heart, along with understanding of wisdom, but it is not understood in the hearts of fools.
Righteousness raises up a nation, but sins diminish peoples.
A wise servant is acceptable to a king, and through his resourcefulness he removes his disgrace.
Anger destroys even the wise. A word spoken at the right time turns away anger, but a hurtful word stirs up anger.
The tongue of the wise knows what is good, but the mouth of fools knows what is evil.
God’s eyes watch everywhere over the evil and the good.
A healing tongue is a tree of life, and whoever practices this will eat its fruit.
A fool scorns his father’s instruction, but whoever pays attention to rebukes is wiser.

There is great strength in abundant righteousness, but the thoughts of the ungodly will be uprooted along with their roots. There is great strength in the house of the righteous, but the fruits of the ungodly will perish.
The lips of the wise are bound to understanding, but the hearts of fools are not firm.
The sacrifices of the lawless are detestable to the Lord, but the sacrifices of the upright are acceptable to him.
The ways of the ungodly are detestable to the Lord, but he loves those who pursue righteousness.
The instruction of the innocent is recognized by passersby, but those who hate rebukes will die in disgrace.
If the underworld and the abyss are exposed before God, how could the hearts of people not be exposed as well?
An uninstructed person does not love the one who rebukes him, and he does not speak with the wise.
A joyful heart makes the face cheerful, but it grows gloomy amid sorrows.
An upright heart seeks understanding, but the mouth of the uninstructed will gather evil things. The heart of a fool knows evil things.
The eyes of the wicked always look ahead for evil things, but the good are always at peace.
A little with fear of the Lord is better than a great treasure without fear.
Hospitality with vegetables, offered with friendship and kindness, is better than fattened calves served with hostility.
An angry person prepares conflicts, but a patient person heals others who fall ill. A patient person puts an end to disputes, but an ungodly person stirs them up all the more.
The paths of the lazy are strewn with thorns, but those of the courageous are smooth.
A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son scorns his mother.
The ways of a fool lack wisdom, but a wise person walks uprightly.
Those who do not honor assemblies abandon counsel, but counsel endures in the hearts of thoughtful people.
An evil person will not listen to it, nor will he say anything good to the people at the proper time.
The thoughts of the wise are paths of life, so that he may turn away from the underworld and be saved.
God will tear down the houses of those who insult others, but he has established the widow’s boundaries.
A thought of injustice is detestable to the Lord, but pure words express understanding.
Whoever accepts a bribe will destroy himself, but whoever hates accepting bribes will live. Sins are forgiven through mercy and faithfulness, and through fear of God everyone turns away from evil.
The hearts of the righteous meditate on faith, but the mouths of the ungodly will speak evil things. The ways of a righteous person are pleasing to God, and through them enemies are reconciled.

God is far from the ungodly, but he listens to the prayers of the righteous. Receiving a little with righteousness is better than a large harvest obtained through injustice. Let a person's heart consider truthful things, so that their ways may be straightened by the Lord.
An eye that sees what is good makes the heart glad, and good news strengthens the bones.
Anyone who abandons instruction despises themselves, but anyone who pays attention to correction loves their own soul.

The fear of the Lord is instruction and wisdom, and the beginning of glory will answer it. Glory will walk with the humble, and the beginning of glory is the foremost righteousness of the upright God.
All the deeds of the humble are plain to God, but the ungodly will perish on an evil day.
Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to God, and anyone who helps another commit injustice will not be acquitted.
The beginning of the good way is to act truthfully, for righteousness is more pleasing to God than the sacrifice of the lawless.
Whoever seeks God will find knowledge in righteousness, and whoever seeks him with uprightness will find peace.
All God's deeds are done in righteousness, but the ungodly are kept for an evil day.
An oracle is on the king's lips, and his mouth will not go astray in judgment.
The balance of the scales is righteousness before God, and every measure in his hand is holy. His deeds are true measures, and the Lord loves upright words.
Anyone who does evil is detestable to a king, for a king's throne is established through righteousness.
Truthful thoughts are pleasing to a king, and God loves truthful deeds.
A king's anger is a messenger of death, but a wise person appeases him.

The king's friends are in the light of life, and those accepted by him are like a cloud bringing the late rain. The king's cheerful face is life, and he benefits those with whom he is pleased like a cloud bringing the late rain.
The dwelling places of wisdom are better than gold, and the dwelling places of understanding are better than choice silver.

The way of life is to turn away from evil, and the paths of righteousness are a long life. Whoever has learned instruction will enjoy good things, and whoever pays attention to correction is wiser still. Whoever guards their ways guards their soul, and whoever loves life will be careful with it.
Disgrace goes before destruction, and evil thoughts go before a fall.
A person who does not become angry, living in righteousness and humility, is better than someone who divides plunder with insolent people.
An understanding person finds good through their deeds, and whoever trusts in the Lord will be blessed.
The wise and intelligent are called discerning, and people listen more readily to those whose speech is pleasant.
Good understanding is a fountain of life to those who have acquired it, but the instruction of fools is bad.
The heart of a wise person understands what comes out of their mouth, and they will carry knowledge on their lips.
Words of wisdom are honeycombs, and the sweetness of hearing them is healing for the soul.
There is a way that a person thinks is straight, but its end leads to the pit of [?].
A strong man endures hardship amid troubles and is constrained by his own ruin, but a crooked person brings about his own ruin with his mouth.
A foolish man digs up evil for himself and gathers fire on his lips.
A crooked man spreads strife, lights a torch of deceit for the wicked, and separates friends.
A lawless man entices his friends and leads them along paths that are not good.
Someone who fixes his eyes is planning deceit, and he also bites his lips. This is a furnace of wickedness.
A good old age is a crown of splendor, and it is found along the paths of righteousness.
A patient man is better than a strong man, and someone who controls his anger is better than someone who captures a city.
They will cast everything into the lap of the oppressors, but justice will be given to everyone by God.
Bread in peace is better than houses full of slaughtered animals amid oppression.
A wise servant rules over foolish masters and divides portions among brothers.
Just as gold and silver are tested in a furnace, so God examines human hearts.
The wicked person listens to the tongues of the lawless, but the righteous person pays no attention to lying lips.

The whole world and its wealth belong to the faithful person, but the unfaithful person does not have even a penny. Grandchildren are the crown of the elderly, and parents are the glory of their children.

Someone who mocks a poor person insults his Maker, and someone who rejoices over another person's destruction will not escape evil. Trustworthy lips do not suit fools, nor do lying lips suit the righteous.
Instruction is a gracious reward for those who practice it; the place it turns toward will be set right.
Someone who conceals wrongs seeks friendship, but someone who hates concealing them separates friends and members of a household.
A rebuke breaks the heart of a wise person, but when a fool is flogged, he does not feel it.
All wicked people stir up uproars, but God will send them a merciless angel.
Anxiety will overtake a wise person, but fools think about evil things.
If someone repays good with evil, evil will not budge from his house.
The beginning of righteousness grants authority, but unrest and fighting go before poverty.
Someone who judges a righteous person to be unrighteous, and someone who judges an unrighteous person to be righteous—both are detestable before the Lord.
Why does a fool have money? For a fool cannot acquire wisdom. Whoever raises his house high seeks destruction, and whoever is perverse in receiving instruction will fall into trouble.
Let your friend be there for you everywhere, and let your brothers be useful to you in your times of need, for they were born for this purpose.
A foolish man claps and rejoices over himself as he guarantees his friends' debts, but a wise person stays away from guaranteeing debts and shows respect.
Someone who loves sin rejoices in fights.
An obstinate person will not meet with good, and a man whose tongue shifts back and forth will fall into evil.
A foolish heart is a heartache to the one who fathered him. No father will rejoice over an uneducated son, but a wise son will make his mother rejoice.
The hearts of those who rejoice give them rest, but the bones of a sorrowful person will dry up.
Someone who accepts a gift into his lap is ungodly, for he will turn away from the paths of righteousness.
The face of a sensible person is wise, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth.
A foolish son brings anger to his father and heartache to the woman who bore him.
It is not good to harm a righteous person, and it is not right to plot against righteous rulers.
Someone who firmly restrains his words is wise, and a patient person is wise. If a fool seeks wisdom,
he will be counted as wise. He will be silent, and you will find him to be wise.
Someone who wants to separate from his friends seeks an excuse. Such a person will always be subject to reproach.
A fool has no need of wisdom, for he prefers foolishness.
When an ungodly person comes into a multitude of evils, he becomes contemptuous, and disgrace and reproach come upon him.
The word in a person's heart is deep water, but the spring of wisdom bubbles and wells up; it cannot be hidden.
It is not good to show favoritism to an ungodly person, and it is not right to turn a righteous person away in judgment.
A fool’s lips will bring him into evils, and his harsh mouth calls upon death.
A fool’s mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a trap for his soul.
Fear brings down the lazy person, and the souls of the fainthearted will go hungry.

Someone who does not correct himself in his actions is the brother of someone who destroys himself. If a fool feels shame, it will be counted as wisdom for him, as it will for someone who corrects himself in his own actions.
The name of the Lord is revealed in the greatness of his power, and the righteous will be exalted by running to him.
A rich man’s wealth is a fortified city, and its glory casts a very great shadow.
A person’s heart becomes proud before his ruin, and it becomes humble before honor.
For someone to speak before listening is foolishness and reproach to him.
A wise servant calms a person’s anger, but who can put up with a fainthearted person?
The heart of the wise will acquire understanding for him, and the ears of the wise seek knowledge.
A person’s gifts make room for him and introduce him to great people.
The righteous person accuses himself at the beginning of his speech, but his opponent will be reproved when he attacks him.
Casting lots settles disputes and makes a division among great people.
A brother helped by a brother is like a strong and lofty city, and he is as powerful as a firmly established kingdom.
A person will fill his stomach with the fruits of his mouth, and he will be satisfied with the fruits of his lips.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who control it will eat its fruit.

Whoever has found a good wife has found a blessing and received favor from God. Whoever drives away a good wife drives away good things. But whoever lives with an adulterous wife is foolish and ungodly.
A person's foolishness ruins his ways, yet in his heart he blames God.
Wealth produces many friends, but the poor person is separated even from his neighbor.
False testimony will not escape punishment, and whoever makes an unjust accusation will not escape.
Many serve in the presence of kings, but all evils will become a reproach to a person.

A good thought draws near to those who know it, and a wise person will find it. Whoever hates a poor brother will also be far from friendship. Whoever does much evil will bring wickedness to completion, and whoever provokes others with words will not escape.
Whoever acquires understanding loves himself, and whoever preserves wisdom will find what is good.
No unjust testimony will escape punishment, and whoever kindles wickedness will perish through it.
Luxury does a fool no good, and if a slave takes charge of a matter, he will take flight in disgrace.
A merciful person is patient, and his glory comes upon those who break the law.
A king's threat is like a lion's roar, but his favor is like dew on grass.
A foolish son is a disgrace to his father, and vows made from a prostitute's earnings are not good.
Parents divide a house and possessions among their children, who inherit them, but a man's wife comes from God.
Weakness takes hold of the fainthearted, and idle people will go hungry.
Whoever keeps the commandment will preserve his life, but whoever disregards his ways will die.
Whoever shows mercy to a poor person lends money to God, and God will repay him according to what he has given. For everyone will receive according to their deeds.
Discipline your son, for in this way he will grow. But do not become arrogant in your heart and act insultingly.
Whoever plans evil will suffer great loss, and if he defiles himself, he will add his life to the loss.
My son, listen to your father's instruction, so that you may be wise in your latter days.
There are many thoughts in a person's heart, but God's plan is what stands firm.
Mercy is fruit beyond counting. A righteous poor person is better than a rich liar.
Fear of the Lord leads to life, and devotion to God leads to a person's life. But whoever has no fear will be in places where [?] no inquiry has ever been made.
Whoever unjustly hides his hands in his lap will not even bring them to his mouth.
Amid hardships a fool goads himself on even more, but if you rebuke a wise person, he will gain understanding.
The son who insults his father and abandons his mother will suffer reproach and disgrace.
A child who abandons instruction will attend to evil things and study hateful words.
Whoever stands surety for a foolish slave insults the law, and the mouth of the ungodly will swallow insults.
Whips will be prepared for the undisciplined, and punishments in the houses of fools.
Wine is unruly, and strong drink is insolent. Anyone who becomes entangled in these will not be wise.
A king’s threat is no different from a lion’s rage. Whoever provokes him and contends with him sins against his own life.
It is a person’s honor to keep away from insults, but every fool becomes entangled in them.
Lazy people are not ashamed when someone reproaches them. The same is true of someone who borrows grain at harvest.
Counsel in a person’s heart is deep water, but a wise person will draw it up.
A person is great, and a merciful person is honored, but finding a faithful person is hard work.
Whoever walks in purity and righteousness will leave his children blessed.
When a righteous king sits on a throne, nothing evil can oppose him.

Who can boast that his heart is pure? Or who can confidently say, “I am free from sin”? The light of someone who speaks evil against his father and mother will be extinguished, and the pupils of his eyes will see darkness. An inheritance acquired hastily at first will not turn out well in the end. Do not say, “I will repay my enemy.” Instead, wait patiently for God to help you.
A large weight and a small one, and two different measures, are both unclean before God.
Whoever does these things will be caught in his own schemes. A young person who walks with someone holy will have a straight path.
The ear hears and the eye sees, and both are God’s works.
Do not love speaking evil, lest you perish. Open your eyes and look at what is right.
Two different weights are an abomination to the Lord, and a dishonest balance is not good in his sight.
A person’s paths are made straight by God. How, then, can a person understand his own paths?
It is a snare for a person to hastily vow away his possessions, for after making the vow he may regret it.
A wise king scatters the ungodly and brings a wheel of harm upon them. Mercy and faithfulness protect a king, and righteous people will surround his throne.
The breath of human beings is the Lord’s light, which searches the body’s innermost chambers.
Mercy and truth guard a king, and righteousness will surround his throne.
Wisdom is the adornment of the young, and knowledge is the glory of the old.
Bruises and wounds will meet evil people, and blows are for their innermost chambers.
Like a stream of water, so the king's heart is in God's hand, and he turns it toward whatever place he wants it to look.
Everyone considers himself justified, but God is the one who sets hearts right.
Doing and speaking what is true are acts of truthfulness that God prefers to sacrificial blood.
A person who is proud and insolent is hard-hearted, and sins are the lamps of the ungodly.
Those who build up treasures with a lying tongue pursue worthless things and come upon the snares of death.
Destruction will overtake the ungodly, for they do not want to do what is right.
The Lord will make the paths of the blameless blameless; his works are pure and upright.
It is better to live in a corner of a roof with a righteous person than to live in plastered rooms and a [?] house amid strife.
There is no mercy in the soul of the ungodly person, nor for those who see it.
When the powerful person suffers loss, the simple person learns more; but the wise person who understands will gain knowledge.
God will destroy the hearts of the ungodly, and he despises the ungodly for their evil deeds.
Anyone who shuts his ears so as not to hear a poor person will himself cry out to God, and God will not hear him.
A gift given in secret turns away anger, but someone who hesitates to give a gift will stir up fierce anger.
Doing justice is the joy of the righteous. But what is pure is unclean [?] evildoers. The lawless person will fall into trouble.
The person who wanders from the paths of righteousness will be among the congregation of the dead.
The poor person loves pleasure, but someone who loves a gift and wealth, throwing it into [?], is ungodly.
The lawless person is the refuse of the righteous person.
It is better to live in the wilderness than to live with a quarrelsome and angry woman.
Choice treasure will be at the mouth of the wise, but foolish people will swallow it up.
The way of righteousness and mercy will find life and honor in peace.
The wise person climbed up into the lofty city and brought down the stronghold in which the ungodly trusted.
Anyone who guards his mouth and his tongue guards his soul.
The stubborn and arrogant person is called a pest. Someone who bears a grudge is lawless.
Desires kill the lazy person, for he will not stretch out his hands to do anything.
The ungodly person craves evil things all day long, but the righteous person shows mercy and compassion without holding back.
The sacrifice of the ungodly is an abomination to the Lord, for they offer their sacrifices unjustly.
A false witness will perish, but an attentive person will speak carefully.
The ungodly person sets his face firmly in shamelessness, but the upright person understands his paths.
Whoever has no wisdom has neither strength nor counsel from God.
A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but help comes from God.
A good name is better than great wealth, and good favor is better than silver. Gold and silver are deceptions of pleasure; excellent favor is better than both of them.
The rich and the poor meet one another, and God made them both.
When a wise person sees evil striking him, he learns all the more. But foolish people pass through it and suffer harm.
Fear of the Lord is the offspring of wisdom, and it produces wealth, honor, and life.
Thorns and traps lie on crooked paths, but whoever guards his soul will keep away from them.
The poor will rule over the rich, and slaves will lend at interest to their own masters.
Whoever sows evil will reap troubles, and he will finish his work under a blow. God will bless the diligent and generous person, and he will bring the blessedness of his work to completion.
Whoever has compassion on a poor person will himself be cared for, because he has given the poor some of his bread. Whoever gives gifts will gain victory and honor. His soul [?] what he has given.
Throw an evil person out of an assembly, so that strife will leave with him. For when he sits among the crowd, he disgraces them all.
God loves pure hearts, and everyone who is pure is chosen by him. The shepherd tends with his lips, and the king is under his authority.
God's eyes guard those who understand, but the lawless person dishonors him with words.
The lazy person finds an excuse and replies, “The lion is on the roads, and people are being killed in the streets.”

The mouth of the lawless is a deep pit, and whoever is hated by God will fall into it. There are evil paths before a person, and he does not like to turn away from them. But you should turn away from every crooked and evil path.
A young boy's heart has leaped with foolishness, for the rod and instruction are far from him.
Whoever wrongs a poor person increases his own troubles, but he will give to the rich at a loss.
Turn your ear toward the words of the wise and listen to my words. Prepare your heart to understand them, because they are good.
And if you keep them in your heart, you will benefit. Set them together upon your lips,
so that you may have confidence in God and he may show you his way.
You too, write them down for yourself three times, with counsel and knowledge.
I teach you to know the truth and to speak truthful words to those who question you. Counsel is harder than the [?] of water. Listen so that you can answer those who question you.
Do not wrong a poor person because he is needy, and do not oppress a weak person at the gates.
For the Lord will judge his case, and you will save your soul unharmed.
Do not befriend an angry person, and do not associate with a hot-tempered companion,
lest you learn his ways and bring a snare upon your soul.
Do not make yourself a guarantor out of embarrassment before someone.
For if you have nothing to pay, they will take the bedding from under your ribs.
Do not move the age-old boundaries that your ancestors established.
An attentive man who is quick in his work should stand before kings, not before weak men.
When you sit down to eat at a ruler’s table, carefully consider what is placed before you.
And reach out your hand toward it, knowing that you will prepare such things.
If you are insatiable, do not crave his food, for these things belong to a deceptive life.
Do not reach out your hand alongside a rich man when you are poor. Instead, keep away from him in your heart.

If you fix your eye on him, he will be nowhere to be seen, for he has prepared wings for himself like an eagle in the air, and he will return to his master’s house. A stone is heavy, and sand is difficult to carry, but a fool’s anger is heavier than both.
Do not eat with an envious man, and do not crave his food.
For he will eat and drink like someone about to swallow a hair.
Do not bring him into your house, lest you eat your bread with him, for he will vomit it up and spoil your pleasant words.
Do not say anything in a fool’s hearing, lest he mock your words.
Do not enter an orphan’s field.
For the mighty God is the one who rescues them, and he will judge you on their behalf.
Apply your heart to instruction and prepare your ears for words of understanding.
Do not stop disciplining a child, for if you strike him with a rod, he will not die.
For you will indeed strike your son with a rod, but you will save his soul from death.
My son, if your heart becomes wise, you will make my heart rejoice too.
And my lips will speak with your lips if they are upright.
Do not let your heart envy sinners. Instead, grow in devotion to God and remain in the fear of the Lord all day long.
For if you observe these things, you will have descendants, and your hope will not fail.
Listen, my son, and become wise, and form upright thoughts in your heart.
Do not be a drunkard, and do not reach out your hand to contribute toward buying meat.
For every drunkard and everyone who visits prostitutes will become poor, and every wine drinker will dress in rags.
My son, listen to your father who brought you into the world, and do not despise your mother because she has grown old.
A righteous father provides good care, and his heart rejoices over a wise son.
Let your father and mother rejoice over you, and let the woman who bore you be glad.
My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes watch over my ways.
For a house that is not yours is a jar full of holes, and it is a narrow pit that is hard to climb out of.
For it will soon be destroyed, and every lawless person will perish.
Who has woe? Who has turmoil? Who has disputes? Who has all kinds of evil talk? Who has wounds for no reason? Or whose eyes are bruised?
Is it not those who linger over wine? Is it not those who ask, “Where will the drinking places be?”
Do not get drunk on wine. Instead, talk with people, and talk with those who are walking about. For if you fix your eyes on the bowls and cups, afterward you will walk about more naked than a pestle.
In the end, you will be like someone who died from a snakebite, and like someone struck by a horned viper, with its venom spreading through him.
If your eyes look at things that are not yours, your mouth will say twisted things.
You will lie down like someone in the middle of the sea, and like a sailor in a great storm.
You will say, “They were hitting me, but I felt no pain. They were laughing at me, but I did not know it. When will dawn come, so that I can go and look for those I will gather with?”
Do not envy evil people, and do not wish to be with them.
Their hearts dwell on deceit, and their lips speak of trouble.
A house is built with wisdom and made to stand firm with understanding.
Through knowledge, the storerooms are filled with every kind of precious and beautiful wealth.
A wise person is better than a strong person, and an intelligent person is better than a large farm.
War is waged with guidance, and help is in the hearts of those who take counsel.
Wisdom and good judgment are at the gates of the wise.
The wise do not express their thoughts aloud in a crowd. Death will meet the uneducated.
The fool will die in sins, and impurity will overwhelm a corrupt person.
On an evil day and a day of distress, until he perishes.
Rescue those being led to death, and do not hold back from redeeming those being killed.
But if you say, "I do not know this," understand that the Lord knows everyone's heart, and the one who formed everyone's breath knows them all. He will repay each person according to their deeds.
My son, eat honey, for the honeycomb is good, so that your palate may be sweetened.
For in this way you will perceive wisdom in your heart. If you find it, your death will be good, and your hope will not perish.
Do not bring an ungodly person into your tent of the righteous, and do not let yourself be deceived by a full belly.
For the righteous person will fall seven times and rise again, but the ungodly will fall into troubles.
If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and do not exalt yourself when he stumbles.
Lest the Lord see it and be displeased, and turn his anger away from him.
Do not rejoice over the evildoer, and do not envy sinners.
For [?] happens to the wicked, and the light of the ungodly will go out forever.
My son, fear God and the king, and do not sin against either of them.

For the ungodly will be punished suddenly. Who can understand the punishments of them both? The son who keeps the word will be saved from destruction, but whoever welcomes destruction has brought it upon himself. Whoever does not teach his son beforehand to guard himself against evil will suddenly grieve. Do not tell the king any lie with your tongue, and let no lie come out of your tongue. For a king’s tongue is a sword, and whatever is given to it is not flesh: he will crush it. For if his anger is provoked, he will destroy human beings. He will devour human bones and burn them like fire, so that young vultures cannot eat them.
I therefore say these things to you, the wise, so that you may understand: showing favoritism in judgment is not good, nor is plotting against someone holy.
Whoever says, “The ungodly person is righteous,” will be cursed among the peoples and hated among the nations.
But honor belongs to those who rebuke, and a good blessing comes upon them.
But lips that speak good words will be loved.
Prepare your work for your journey, and make yourself ready for your field. Follow me, and you will build your house.
Do not give false testimony against your neighbor, and do not be deceitful with your lips.
Do not say, “I will do to him just as he did to me; I will repay him for the wrongs he did to me.”
The senseless person is like a field, and the uneducated person is like a garden.
If you leave it alone, it will become barren, entirely overgrown with nettles, and deserted, and its stone fences will be torn down.
Afterward I reconsidered. I looked, to receive instruction. How long will you lie there, sluggard? When will you rise from sleep?
A little while, and you turn over; a little while, and you sleep; a little while, and you fold your hands against your chest.
But if you do this, poverty will come walking toward you, and need will come like a good runner.
These are the unclassified teachings of Solomon, which the companions of Hezekiah, king of Judea, wrote down.
The glory of God is to conceal a matter, but the glory of the king is to honor his deeds.
Heaven is high, the earth is deep, and the hearts of kings cannot be understood.
Beat impure silver so that it becomes completely pure.
[?] before the king, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
Do not exalt yourself before a king, and do not stand in the place of powerful people.
For it is better for someone to tell you, “Come up here,” than for you to be humbled before powerful people. Look at them,
so that they do not catch you hastily involved in a quarrel, and so that you do not regret it in the end, when your companion reproaches you.
Withdraw from him; do not treat him with contempt.

Do not let your friend reproach you. Strife and hostility will not depart from you, but will be like death to you. Preserve goodwill and friendship for yourself in freedom, so that you do not become an object of reproach; instead, keep your ways orderly.
Like a golden apple in a necklace of carnelian, so is a valued word spoken to a receptive ear.
A golden earring with a precious carnelian set in it: so are the words of the wise to a listening ear.
Like the coolness of snow at harvest, which refreshes a threshing floor, so is a faithful messenger to those who send him, for he benefits the souls of those for whom he carries out an errand.
Like winds, clouds, and rains appearing, so are those who boast of a false gift.
Receive kings with patience, but an angry tongue crushes bones.
If you find honey, eat only enough for yourself, lest you become full and vomit.
Do not visit your friend too often, lest he become tired of you and hate you.
Like a club, a sword, and a sharp arrow, so is a person who gives false testimony against his friend.
The way of the evil person and the foot of the lawless person will be ruined on an evil day.
As vinegar is bad for a wound, so an illness in the body grieves the heart. Like a moth in clothing and a worm in wood, so a person's sorrow harms his heart.
If your enemy is hungry, feed him, and if he is thirsty, give him something to drink.
For by doing this you will heap burning coals on his head, and God will repay you with good things.
A north wind stirs up clouds, and a shameless face provokes tongues.
It is better to live on a corner of a roof than to live in a new house with a woman who curses.
[?] is cool to a thirsty soul, and good news from far away.
Like someone who blocks a spring of water and spoils flowing water, doing violence, so is someone who humiliates a righteous person before an ungodly person.
It is not good to eat much honey, but it is right to honor honorable words.
Like a city whose walls have been demolished, so is a person who does not act with counsel.
Like dew at harvest and rain in summer, which are not valued, so a fool has no honor.
Like birds and sparrows in flight, so an empty curse does not come upon anyone.
A whip for a horse, a bridle for a donkey, and a club for a foolish nation.
Do not answer a fool according to his foolishness, so that you do not become like him.
Instead, answer a fool in opposition to his foolishness, so that he does not appear wise in his own eyes.
And he brings disgrace through his words when you send a message through a foolish messenger.
Take away the path of his foot, and a proverb from the mouths of fools.
Like someone who ties a stone in a sling, so is someone who gives honor to a fool.
Thorns grow in the hands of a drunkard, and slavery in the hands of fools.
Everyone laughs at fools, for their way will lead to ruin.
Just as a dog returns to its vomit and is loathed, so a fool returns to his sin in his wickedness. There is a shame that produces sin, and there is a shame that brings honor and favor.
I saw a man who considered himself wise, but a fool has more hope than he does.
When a lazy person is sent on a journey, he says, “There is a lion in the streets, and people are being killed in the squares.”
As a door turns on its hinge, so a lazy person turns on his bed.
A lazy person hides his hands in his lap and cannot bring them to his mouth.
A lazy person considers himself wiser than an educated person who gives an answer.
Like someone who grabs a dog is someone who takes a stand before a dispute that is not his own.
Like angry people who hurl words, the first [?] will stumble.
So it is with everyone who deceives their neighbors: when they are caught, they say, “I did it as a joke.”
A fire burns with plenty of wood, but fighting will stop where there is no angry person.
Coals are for a hearth, and wood is for a fire; a person who curses stirs up a fight.
The words of a gossip are gentle, but they strike deep into the chambers of the heart.
Silver given deceitfully is like pieces of broken pottery; deceitful lips cover a troubled heart.
An enemy answers everyone with assent on his lips, but in his heart he thinks of deceit.
If your enemy pleads with you in a gentle voice, do not listen to him, for there are seven kinds of wickedness in his heart.
Someone who hides hostility stirs up wickedness, but a wise person exposes his sins in an assembly.
Someone who digs a pit for his neighbor will fall into it, and someone who rolls a stone will have it fall on him.
A lying tongue hates the truth, and a disruptive mouth will cause disturbances.
Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what tomorrow will bring.
Let another mouth praise you, not your own—a stranger, and not your own lips.
A stone is heavy, and sand is hard to lift, but a fool’s anger is heavier than both.
Rage is merciless, and anger is harsh, but no one can endure jealousy.
Open rebukes are better than hidden friendship.
A friend’s wounds are better than an enemy’s kisses.
A satisfied soul scorns a honeycomb, but even bitter things are sweet to a hungry soul.
Like a bird that flies away from its nest, so a person becomes a slave when he wanders away from his own place.
The heart rejoices in perfumes, wine, and incense, but the heart collapses in sickness.
Do not abandon a wise friend or your father's friend. Do not enter your brother's house when you are in distress. A friend nearby is better than a brother far away from you.
Be wise, my son, so that my heart may rejoice, and turn insulting words away from yourself.
A wise person hides from approaching evils, but fools encounter them and suffer harm.
Take your cloak, for the mocker passes you by, for he mocks others.
Someone who blesses his friend loudly in the morning is no different from someone who curses him.
Rain drives a person out of his house during the cold days. So does a cursing wife in your own house.
The north wind is harsh, yet it is called “the upright one.”
Iron sharpens iron, and a person sharpens his friend's face.
Someone who plants a fig tree will eat its fruit, and someone who looks after his master will receive honor.
Just as faces do not resemble one another, so people's hearts do not resemble one another.

The underworld and destruction are never satisfied. Likewise, the eyes of oppressive people are never satisfied. Brazen eyes and undisciplined people who do not control their tongues are an abomination to the Lord.
The furnace tests silver and gold, but a person is tested through the mouths of those who speak about him. The heart of a lawless person seeks evil things, but an upright heart seeks knowledge.
Even if you whip a fool in the midst of a crowd, humiliating him, you will not remove his foolishness.
Know well the lives of your livestock, and set your heart on your herds.
For a person's strength and authority do not last forever, nor is authority handed down from generation to generation.
Take care of the vegetation growing in the field so that you may harvest it early and gather grass in its season.
Then you will have sheep for clothing. Take care of your field so that you will have goats.
My son, I have given you important words for your life and for the life of your servants.
An ungodly person runs away when no one is pursuing him, but a righteous person is steadfast like a lion.
Judgments arise because of the sins of the ungodly, but a wise person will put out the flames of anger.
Someone who is strong in his wickedness slanders a poor person, like heavy rain that does no good.
