So it is with those who abandon the law: they honor wickedness. But those who love the law set a wall against them.
Evil people will not understand justice, but those who seek the Lord will understand every good thing.
A poor person who walks in truth is better than a rich liar.
A wise son keeps the law, but one who lives extravagantly brings shame on his father.
Those who have mercy on the poor will gather the wealth of someone who increases it by charging interest.
The prayer of someone who turns his ear away from hearing the law is an abomination.
Someone who leads the upright astray onto an evil path will himself fall into troubles, but the holy will share in good things.
A rich person is wise in his own eyes, but a wise poor person will find fault with him.
Great glory comes through the help of the righteous, but people perish where the ungodly are.
Someone who hides his wrongdoing will not prosper, but someone who admits it and rebukes it will be loved.
Blessed is the person who respects everyone out of fear, but the hardhearted person will fall into troubles.
A poor person who rules over a multitude of poor people is a hungry lion and a thirsty wolf.
A king who lacks money is a great oppressor, but those who hate oppression will live a long time.
Someone who stands surety for a person accused of murder will flee and will not be secure. But someone who walks uprightly will be helped.
But someone who walks on crooked paths will stumble.
Someone who works his land will have enough bread, but someone who pursues idleness will have his fill of poverty.
A wise person will receive abundant blessings, but an evildoer will not escape evil.
Someone who shows deference to oppressors will not prosper, for such a person will sell a person for a loaf of bread.

An envious person hurries to become rich and does not know that a merciful person will rule over him. Someone who increases his wealth by charging interest will gather it for someone who has mercy on the poor.
Someone who rebukes a person for his ways will find more favor than someone who flatters him with his tongue.
Someone who robs his father and mother, thinking, “I am not sinning,” is the companion of an ungodly person.
An insatiable person judges rashly, but someone who trusts in the Lord will be protected.
Someone who trusts in stubbornness is foolish, but someone who walks in wisdom will be saved.
Someone who gives to the poor will not lack anything, but someone who turns his eyes away from them will suffer great want.
The righteous groan where the ungodly are, but they flourish when those people perish.
A person who rebukes is better than a stubborn person, for the latter will suddenly burn and will not be healed.
The peoples will rejoice when they speak of the righteous, but people will groan under the rule of the ungodly.
The father of a person who seeks wisdom will rejoice, but anyone who lives in sexual immorality will destroy his wealth.
A righteous king builds up a country, but a lawless person tears it down.
Anyone who prepares a net in front of his companion will spread it out for his own feet.
A great trap awaits the sinful person, but the righteous person will have joy and gladness.
The righteous person knows how to judge the poor, but the ungodly person will not understand knowledge, and the poor person has no understanding.
Evil people burn down a city, but the wise turn away anger.
The wise person will judge the nations, but people laugh at the sinner when he becomes angry.
Bloodthirsty people hate the holy person, but the upright seek his life.
The fool pours out all his anger, but the wise person lets it out little by little.
If a king listens to unjust words, all those who serve him are lawless.
The person who lends at interest and the person who borrows meet one another, and God will examine them both.
If a king judges the poor truthfully, his throne will stand as a testimony.
Rods and rebukes give wisdom, but a son who goes astray will bring shame on his father.
Sins increase as the ungodly increase, but when they fall, the righteous become afraid.
Discipline your son, and he will give you gladness and bring delight to your soul.
There will be no greatness for a lawless nation, but blessed is the person who keeps the law.
A stubborn servant will not be taught by words; even if he understands, he will not obey.
If you see someone who is quick to speak, know that a fool has more hope than he does.
Someone who lives in luxury from childhood will become a servant, and afterward he will grieve over himself.
An angry person stirs up strife, and a hotheaded person piles up sin.
Contempt humiliates a person, but honor will raise up the humble.
Anyone who shares with a thief hates his own soul. If an oath is imposed and they do not disclose the matter,
they will fall and be put to shame, because they feared people. But blessed is the person who fears God. Cowardice sets a snare for a person, but anyone who trusts in the Lord will be safe.
Many serve in the presence of the great, but a person's justice comes from God.

The righteous person is detestable to the oppressor, and the way of sinners is detestable to the righteous person. The oppressor is unclean in the presence of the righteous person, and the righteous person is held in contempt in the presence of the ungodly.
My son, fear my words, and when you have accepted them, repent. These are the things a person says to those who trust in God: “I will stop.
For I am wiser than any person, and the wisdom within me is not human wisdom.”
God is the one who taught me wisdom, and I have learned the knowledge of the holy ones.

Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in his fist? Who has gathered the water in his garment? Who has taken hold of the ends of the earth? What is his name, or the name of his children?
All God's words are choice and refined. Understanding the law is a good thought of mine, and he himself protects those who fear him.
Do not add to his words, or he will rebuke you and you will become a liar.
There are two things I ask of you: do not withdraw your favor from me before I die.
Let empty and lying words be far from me. Give me neither wealth nor poverty. Allot me what I need and what is sufficient for me.
So that I do not become full and turn into a liar and say, “Who sees me?” Or become poor and steal and swear by the name of my God.
Do not hand a slave over to his master, lest he curse you and you be ruined.
An evil son curses his father and does not bless his mother.
An abominable son judges himself to be righteous, but he has not cleansed his way.
An evil son is arrogant. His own commands seem good to him, and he exalts himself with his eyelids.
The teeth of an evil son are swords, and his molars are butchers, destroying the humble of the earth and the poor among people.
The leech has three daughters whom she truly loves, and these three have not satisfied her.
Hades, a woman's desire, Tartarus, and the earth that is never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, “Enough!” And the fourth has never been found saying, “It is sufficient.”
The eye that mocks its father and insults its mother's old age—the ravens in the valleys will peck it out, and the young eagles will eat it.
There are three things that are difficult for me to understand, and the fourth I do not know:
The path of an eagle in flight, the paths of a snake on a rock, the paths of a ship under sail, and the paths of a person in his youth.
Such is the way of an adulterous woman: she does what she does, wipes herself, and says, “I have committed no sin.”
The earth trembles under three things, and it cannot bear the fourth.
When a slave becomes king, and a fool has his fill of bread,
and a slave woman casts out her mistress, and a hated woman obtains a good husband.
There are four very small creatures on the earth, yet they are wiser than the wise:
The ants, which have no strength, yet prepare their food in summer;
and the rock hyraxes, which are a weak nation, yet have made their homes among the rocks.
The locusts have no king over them, yet they march out in formation at a single command.
And the lizard, which holds firmly with its hands and is easy to destroy, lives in kings' houses.
There are three that walk gracefully, and the fourth comes out in formation:
A young lion, mighty among the animals, which does not turn back, and which no animal frightens.
And a rooster walking proudly among hens, and a goat leading a herd of goats, and a king speaking among a large crowd.
My son, if you give yourself over to pleasure and stretch your hand toward your mouth in a quarrel, you will be put to shame.
[?] milk, so that you may obtain butter. But if you squeeze them, blood comes out. And if you draw out words, judgments and quarrels result.
My words were spoken through God. The saying of the king, which his mother taught him.
What you are to observe, my son, are the words of God. I will tell you from the beginning. My son, what is it, son of my womb? What is it, son of my prayers?
Do not give your wealth to women, or your possessions to a belated decision.
Do everything with counsel and a plan. Drink wine with discretion. These great men are prone to anger; do not let them drink wine,
lest they drink and forget wisdom and become unable to judge the weak fairly.
Give strong drink to those in sorrow, and wine to those whose hearts are distressed,
so that they may forget their poverty and no longer remember their troubles.
From now on, open your mouth for the word of God and judge them all for their welfare.
But judge the case of the poor and the weak.
Who will find a strong woman? A woman like this is more precious than valuable stones.
Her husband's heart relies on her. She will not lack bread.
For she does good things for her husband, not bad things, at all times.
She finds wool and flax and works them with her willing hands.
She has become like merchant ships that bring her goods from afar.
And she rises at night and gives food to the members of her household and work to her servants.
When she sees a field, she buys it. She plants vineyards with the proceeds of her hands.
She has girded her waist firmly with strength and strengthened her arms for her work. She has tasted that working is good.
And her lamp does not go out throughout the night.
She stretches out her hand to useful tasks and steadies her arms at the spindle. She opens her hand to a poor person and extends her wrist to someone in need.
Her husband does not worry about the members of the household when he stays somewhere for a long time, for everyone with her is clothed.
She has made two garments for her husband and clothing for herself from fine linen and purple cloth.
People look to her husband at the gates when he sits in an assembly with the elders and those who live in the land.
She has made linen garments and sold them, and belts for the Phoenicians.
She has clothed herself with strength and glory.
She has not eaten the bread of idleness. The paths of her house are narrow, and she will rejoice in the last days.
She will open her mouth with wisdom, and the law of [?] and mercy is on her tongue.
Many women have acquired wealth, and many have done mighty deeds, but you have surpassed them all.
Charms are deceptive, and a woman’s beauty is worthless, for a woman who loves God will be praised. Let her praise the fear of the Lord.
Give her some of the fruit of her hands, so that they may proclaim the fame of her deeds at the entrances to the assemblies, and let them praise her husband at the gates.
